elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 expressly provides that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer, whether or not it constitutes a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The operative language assigns only defined Deliverables and does not mention or otherwise demonstrably include all work product.

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in the Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 uses a present assignment for each Deliverable, but the assignment does not expressly cover other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all Vendor pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 retains only Vendor Technology. Without language or a supplied definition encompassing all pre-existing Vendor intellectual property, the required scope is not complete.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Sections 14.3 and 13.2 grant a licence only for software and Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, not demonstrably all Vendor intellectual property embedded in it.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the applicable licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and grants Vendor only a limited processing right for specified Customer-related purposes.

elements.element: No jointly owned intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned intellectual property is created absent a separate signed instrument; no such instrument is supplied.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its generic tools.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 retains Vendor Technology, but generic tools are not expressly included and no definition establishing that coverage is supplied.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its generic know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly reserve generic know-how, and it is not demonstrably included within the undefined term Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer receives rights in all Deliverables equivalent to a licence.
elements.evidence: Customer receives outright ownership of each Deliverable under Section 14.2, supplemented by the Section 13.2 licence for embedded or required Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: The assignment of ownership has no time limit, and the licence covering embedded or required Vendor Technology is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The ownership assignment contains no revocation right, and the applicable Vendor Technology licence is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The ownership assignment is not territorially limited, and Section 13.2 expressly makes the Vendor Technology licence worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the Deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Customer owns the Deliverables, and Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence for applicable Vendor Technology royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer may use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership permits Customer to use the Deliverables, and Section 13.2 expressly permits use of applicable Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership includes control over modifications, and Section 13.2 expressly permits modification and creation of derivative works from applicable Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Although Customer can license the portions it owns, Section 13.2 permits only contractors to support embedded Vendor Technology and does not grant a general sublicensing right covering that technology.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its rights in the Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's ownership is not purpose-limited, and Section 13.2 expressly permits use of applicable Vendor Technology for Customer's business.

result.reason: The redline makes the targeted ownership reversal and preserves unrelated provisions, but neither level is complete. The preferred position fails because non-Deliverable work product is omitted and the retention/licence provisions cover only Vendor Technology and software rather than demonstrably all pre-existing and embedded Vendor IP. The fallback also fails because generic tools and know-how are not expressly reserved and the embedded Vendor Technology licence lacks a general sublicensing right. Because no complete level is reached, the redline is not minimal as defined. Drafting quality is weak because the broad Deliverable assignment is not expressly carved back for retained Vendor Technology, leaving the relationship between Sections 14.2 and 14.3 dependent on implication.
